name: Kohima
description: Capital of Nagaland and headquarters of Kohima district, a scenic hill town at about 1,444 m elevation known for its Angami Naga culture, local markets, and as the base for exploring nearby heritage villages, war sites and valleys. Gateway for the Hornbill Festival circuit and western Nagaland.
facts: Capital of Nagaland and HQ of Kohima district
Elevation around 1,444 m
Site of the 1944 Battle of Kohima
Nearest airport and rail at Dimapur ~74 km
Best season October to April

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill in the heart of Kohima, commemorating the 1944 Battle of Kohima that halted the Japanese advance into India. Contains 1,420 Commonwealth burials, a cremation memorial for 917 Hindu and Sikh soldiers, and preserves the outline of the historic tennis court where fierce fighting occurred.
facts: Site of the Battle of Kohima, April 1944
1,420 Commonwealth burials of WWII
Memorial to 917 cremated Hindu and Sikh soldiers
Famous epitaph: 'When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today'
Open daily 09:00-16:00

name: Kisama Heritage Village (Naga Heritage Village)
description: Open-air heritage complex about 12 km south of Kohima between Kigwema and Phesama, designed as a traditional Naga village with morungs representing all major Naga ethnic groups. Primary venue of the annual Hornbill Festival (1-10 December) showcasing tribal culture, dances, crafts and cuisine.
facts: Venue of the Hornbill Festival every December 1-10
Houses morungs of 16-17 Naga ethnic groups
About 12 km south of Kohima on NH2
Living museum of Naga architecture and traditions
Name combines Kigwema and Phesama

name: Khonoma (Green Village)
description: Western Angami Naga village about 20 km west of Kohima, widely known as India’s first green village for its community conservation efforts. Features terraced paddy fields, traditional stone architecture, the Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth’s tragopan, and homestays for immersive cultural experiences.
facts: India’s first green village (declared ~2005)
About 20 km west of Kohima
Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protects Blyth’s tragopan
Elevation around 1,500-1,600 m
Strong community-based eco-tourism and homestays

name: Dzukou Valley (Dzükou Valley)
description: High-altitude alpine valley straddling the Nagaland-Manipur border at about 2,438-2,452 m elevation, renowned for rolling meadows of dwarf bamboo, seasonal wildflowers (including the Dzukou lily), streams and panoramic views. Popular trekking destination accessed from Viswema or Jakhama; often called the Valley of Flowers of the Northeast.
facts: Elevation around 2,438-2,452 m
Straddles Kohima district (Nagaland) and Senapati (Manipur)
Famous for seasonal blooms and Dzukou lily
Best accessed by trek from Viswema/Jakhama
Popular for camping and nature photography

name: Japfu Peak (Mount Japfü)
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima. Offers challenging treks with panoramic views, home to the world’s tallest rhododendron tree (Guinness record), and habitat for rare birds including Blyth’s tragopan. Best climbed November to March.
facts: Elevation 3,048 m; second highest in Nagaland
About 15 km south of Kohima
Holds Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree (~20 m+)
Trek starts near Kigwema; guide recommended
Views over Dzukou Valley and surrounding ranges

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum on Bayavü Hill in Kohima, established in 1970, showcasing ethnographic collections of Naga tribal artefacts, traditional dresses, ornaments, weapons, musical instruments, wood carvings and models of Naga houses. Essential introduction to the cultural diversity of Nagaland’s ethnic groups.
facts: Opened to public on 25 November 1970
Located on Bayavü Hill, about 1.5-2 km from town centre
Operated by Department of Art and Culture
Displays artefacts from multiple Naga tribes
Key starting point for understanding Naga heritage

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral (Kohima Cathedral)
description: Catholic cathedral on Aradura Hill blending traditional Naga house architecture with modern design, featuring a 16-foot carved wooden crucifix among Asia’s largest. Consecrated in 1991; construction largely funded by Japanese contributors as a memorial related to the Battle of Kohima. Capacity around 4,500.
facts: Consecrated January 1991
Blends Naga traditional architecture
16-ft carved wood crucifix
Partly funded by Japanese as WWII memorial gesture
Main church of the Diocese of Kohima

name: Dzüleke (Dzuleke)
description: Small Angami Naga eco-tourism village in the Western Angami hills about 30-40 km from Kohima, known for community conservation (hunting ban since 1999), pristine forests, streams, homestays and quiet nature experiences. Population around 156; ideal for slow, offbeat village stays.
facts: About 30-40 km from Kohima
Community banned hunting/trapping in 1999
Population ~156 (Census 2011)
Eco-tourism board and homestays supported by NEIDA/Tata Trusts
Elevation around 1,800-2,100 m

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-run model tourist village about 36-41 km north of Kohima, recreating a traditional Angami Naga settlement with thatched huts, community kitchen, cultural performances and panoramic hill views. Developed with Nagaland Tourism for immersive cultural stays and experiences.
facts: About 36-41 km from Kohima on the Wokha/Dimapur road
Community-based tourism project since early 2000s
Traditional thatched cottages and local cuisine
Cultural performances and bonfires
Official district tourist place
